text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Government may propose cap on bus fare increases to ensure no sudden hikes.
- India's President Shankar Dayal Sharma refuses to install new minority coalition government until Congress Party convinces him committed to arrangement.
- North Korean defector Hwang Jang Yop arrives in South Korea with mission to stop Pyongyang from launching war.
- Standard Chartered Bank next to introduce "low-start repayment" housing loans for borrowers with low monthly instalments that increase over loan period.
- Analysts say more Japanese banks expected to close their foreign operations within next few years as enormous problem loans have caused difficulties for banks in meeting new capital requirements.
- Group of Seven leading industrial nations to agree later this week to curb greenback's rise.
- Prices of DRAM chips have risen about 50 percent in last few months making economists uncertain increase can be sustained.
- Former socialist Inder Kumar Gujral appointed India's 12th prime minister after he was elected leader of 13-party ruling United Front coalition.
- Singapore restaurants do not always share 10 percent service charge levy with employees, Business Times finds.
- Neptune Orient Lines management sees limited pressure on container liner margins although May 1 industry conference seems to be crucial to future direction of rates.
- Securities Commission of Malaysia and China Securities Regulatory Commission sign pact on cooperation.
